seniorPensionSchemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (LIC)
seniorPensionSchemes.statusNote: PMVVY subscription window closed on 31 March 2023 and has not been extended by the Ministry of Finance. Existing policyholders continue to receive their assured 7.40% p.a. monthly pension until completion of their 10-year policy term. Senior citizens seeking sovereign regular income can consider SCSS (8.20% p.a., ₹30L cap) or RBI Floating Rate Savings Bonds (8.05% p.a.).
seniorPensionSchemes.sovereignIssuer: LIC of India / Govt of India
seniorPensionSchemes.existingHoldersNote: For existing subscribers only (policies issued up to 31 Mar 2023).

seniorPensionSchemes.name: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (Post Office / Banks)
seniorPensionSchemes.statusNote: Sovereign quarterly-payout deposit for individuals aged 60+ (55+ for retirees, 50+ for retired defence personnel). Maximum limit enhanced to ₹30 Lakh per individual. Eligible for Section 80C (Section 123 of Income-tax Act 2025) deduction under the Old Tax Regime.
seniorPensionSchemes.sovereignIssuer: Ministry of Finance / India Post & Authorised Banks
seniorPensionSchemes.existingHoldersNote: Extendable in 3-year blocks after initial 5-year maturity.

seniorPensionSchemes.name: RBI Floating Rate Savings Bonds, 2020 (Taxable)
seniorPensionSchemes.statusNote: 7-year sovereign bond paying interest semi-annually (1 Jan & 1 Jul) pegged at NSC rate + 35 bps (currently 7.70% + 0.35% = 8.05% p.a.). No maximum investment ceiling. Premature encashment permitted for seniors aged 60+ after minimum lock-in.
seniorPensionSchemes.sovereignIssuer: Reserve Bank of India / Govt of India
seniorPensionSchemes.existingHoldersNote: Senior citizens get early lock-in relaxation (6 yrs for age 60-70, 5 yrs for 70-80, 4 yrs for 80+).

seniorPensionSchemes.name: Post Office Monthly Income Scheme
seniorPensionSchemes.statusNote: 5-year Post Office monthly payout deposit open to all resident adults. Enhanced deposit limit of ₹9 Lakh for single accounts and ₹15 Lakh for joint accounts.
seniorPensionSchemes.existingHoldersNote: Joint account limit is ₹15,00,000 across up to 3 joint holders.

notes: RBI Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) reduced the policy repo rate to 5.50% (SDF 5.25%, MSF/Bank Rate 5.75%) and Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) to 3.00% during FY 2025-26/2026-27 easing.

Following the 100 bps cumulative repo reduction, major public and private banks lowered EBLR home loan starting rates (SBI starting at 7.50% p.a.) and revised retail 1Y-5Y FD peak slabs (~6.80% to 7.50% general, +50 bps for seniors).

Ministry of Finance (DEA) kept Small Savings rates unchanged for Q3 FY 2026-27 (1 Oct 2026 – 31 Dec 2026): PPF 7.10%, SSY 8.20%, SCSS 8.20%, NSC 7.70%, POMIS 7.40%, KVP 7.50% (115 months), POTD 1Y 6.90% / 2Y 7.00% / 3Y 7.10% / 5Y 7.50%, and PORD 6.70%.

The Income-tax Act, 2025 took effect on 1 April 2026 (replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961 for Tax Year 2026-27 / AY 2027-28). All numeric tax slabs, standard deductions (₹75,000 New / ₹50,000 Old), rebate limits (₹12,00,000 taxable income / ₹60,000 max rebate in New Regime), and deduction caps (₹1.5L 80C, ₹25k/₹50k 80D, ₹2L 24(b)) remain unchanged, while statutory section numbers now map to Section 202 (New Regime, formerly 115BAC), Section 156 (Tax Rebate, formerly 87A), Section 123 (formerly 80C), Section 126 (formerly 80D), and Section 22(1)(b) (Home Loan Interest, formerly 24(b)).
Banking & financial service charges continue to attract 18% GST under SAC 9971.
